Where in this repo's hooks and scripts does code call `_config_enabled` to check a config-key toggle, as opposed to just mentioning it in a comment?
cases.curator_notes: Built by enumerating every production call site of `_config_enabled` (git grep at the pinned commit, excluding comments, the function's own definition in _config.sh, and test files) and attributing each call line to its enclosing bash function or, when the call sits outside any function, to a single per-file `top-level-main` label. One judgment-call type applied uniformly (function vs. top-level scope), no case needing a second kind of call. config-get.sh is listed as a near-miss because its own comments describe it as delegating to _config_enabled, but its actual call is to the differently-named _config_value.
cases.second_pass_notes: Independently re-derived the full call-site set via git grep at the pinned commit and attributed each to its enclosing function/top-level block. Zero additional sites found; all 13 key entries and the config-get.sh near-miss confirmed by direct read (config-get.sh calls _config_value, not _config_enabled).

cases.question: Where in this repo's hooks and scripts does code call `_lib_marker_value_present` to check whether a review/approval marker is already present?
cases.curator_notes: Built by enumerating every production call site of `_lib_marker_value_present` (git grep at the pinned commit, excluding comments and tests) and attributing each to its enclosing function or top-level block. marker.sh's two call sites (code-review-markers check and verification-markers check) both sit in its top-level case-dispatch body with no enclosing function, so they collapse to one `top-level-main` entry; require-plan-review.sh's three call sites collapse the same way. The two sibling _lib.sh files' own function definitions are listed as near-misses, not keys, since a definition is not a read site.
cases.second_pass_notes: Independently re-derived all 9 production call sites (require-code-review.sh:222, require-plan-review.sh:129/284/318, require-ready-for-review.sh:409, marker.sh:261/1093/1135, require-skill-review.sh:421) and confirmed each attribution by reading the enclosing scope at the pinned commit. Zero additional sites found; zero wrong key entries.

cases.question: Where in this repo's hooks and scripts is a session id validated as a safe filesystem-path component (via `_lib_valid_session_id_component`) before being used to build a marker, state, or log file path?
cases.curator_notes: Built by enumerating every production call site of `_lib_valid_session_id_component` (git grep at the pinned commit, excluding comments, the definition, and tests) and attributing each to its enclosing function or top-level block; a single judgment-call type (function vs. top-level scope) throughout. `_lib_resolve_session_id` is a near-miss: a differently-named sibling in the same file that resolves a live process's session id from scratch rather than validating one already in hand, which a model could plausibly conflate with this question.
cases.second_pass_notes: Confirmed by independent pass; 18 sites. One draft entry moved to accepted_near_misses: it validates the session id but writes to a fixed log path, never using the id as a path component. `_lib_review_pr_select_session_worktrees` also validates the session id but builds a worktree directory name rather than a marker, state, or log path; two reviewers split on whether it is on-topic, so it is scored as neither hit nor false positive.
